scenes.title: The Heart as a Pump
scenes.narration: Every beat begins as an electrical impulse that spreads through the heart. The atria contract first, then the ventricles, in sequence, and blood leaves through the aorta and the pulmonary trunk. About the size of a closed fist, a resting heart beats about 100,000 times a day. It pumps about 5 litres of blood per minute, which is more than 7,000 litres a day.

notes.note: Fist-sized · 250–350 g · about 100,000 beats a day
About 5 litres a minute · more than 7,000 a day

scenes.narration: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae. The right ventricle pumps it to the lungs. The left atrium receives oxygenated blood, and the left ventricle pumps it into the aorta. The interventricular septum separates the two ventricles. Together, the four chambers form one pump.

Blood leaves the right heart along the pulmonary arteries, which carry deoxygenated blood, and reaches the lungs. The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood on to the left heart. The left heart pumps it to the body tissues, and from there it returns to the right heart. The two circuits are in series, so blood passes through one after the other. Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it toward it.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[Right heart]:::blue --> B[Pulmonary arteries]:::blue --> C[Lungs] --> D[Pulmonary veins]:::red --> E[Left heart]:::red --> F[Body tissues] --> A

notes.note: Pulmonary circuit, then systemic circuit: in series
Arteries: away from the heart · veins: toward it

scenes.narration: The left ventricle pumps blood through the aorta to the whole body, at a systolic pressure of about 120 millimetres of mercury. The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary artery at about 25 millimetres of mercury, and serves the lungs only. The left ventricular wall is also about three times thicker than the right.

notes.note: Left ventricular wall: about three times thicker than the right

scenes.narration: The sinoatrial node, the pacemaker, starts the impulse, which spreads over both atria. It then reaches the atrioventricular node, where it is delayed by about 0.1 seconds so that the atria finish contracting. The impulse passes down the bundle of His, into the right and left bundle branches in the septum, and out along the Purkinje fibres. The ventricles contract from the apex upward.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[SA node · right atrium wall]:::teal --> B[Both atria] --> C[AV node · 0.1 s delay]:::red --> D[Bundle of His] --> E[Bundle branches in septum] --> F[Purkinje fibres] --> G[Ventricles contract, apex up]:::blue

scenes.narration: The sinoatrial node fires 60 to 100 times a minute, the atrioventricular node 40 to 60, and the Purkinje fibres 20 to 40. Each has its own intrinsic rate, but the fastest pacemaker sets the rate for the heart. So the sinoatrial node normally leads.

notes.note: The fastest pacemaker sets the rate

scenes.narration: The cycle begins with atrial systole. The ventricles then begin to contract with all valves closed, in isovolumetric contraction. The atrioventricular valves closing make the first heart sound, lub. The semilunar valves then open and the ventricles eject blood. In isovolumetric relaxation, the semilunar valves closing make the second heart sound, dub. The atrioventricular valves open, and the ventricles fill.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[Atrial systole] --> B[Isovolumetric contraction]:::red --> C[S1 lub · AV valves close] --> D[Ventricular ejection]:::red --> E[Isovolumetric relaxation]:::blue --> F[S2 dub · semilunar valves close] --> G[Ventricular filling]

scenes.narration: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume gives cardiac output. At rest the heart rate is about 70 beats per minute, and the stroke volume is about 70 millilitres. Together they give 4,900 millilitres per minute, about 4.9 litres per minute. That is close to the adult's total blood volume of about 5 litres.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[Heart rate · about 70 a minute] --> B[Stroke volume · about 70 mL] --> C[Cardiac output · about 4.9 L a minute]:::red

scenes.narration: The coronary arteries arise from the aortic root, just above the aortic valve. The left anterior descending artery supplies the front of the left ventricle and the septum. The right coronary artery supplies the right heart and, in most people, the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes. The left ventricle is perfused mainly during diastole. If a coronary artery is blocked, the muscle beyond it becomes ischaemic and may suffer myocardial infarction.

To summarise. An electrical impulse makes the atria and then the ventricles contract, driving two circulations in series. At rest the output is about 5 litres per minute. And the heart's own muscle depends on the coronary arteries.

notes.note: An impulse sets the sequence: atria, then ventricles
The heart muscle is fed by the coronary arteries
